question: Can a validation-driven rule for choosing the bin size give a lower attacker identification rate at lower storage cost than a fixed bin size of 16 under the same attacker?
method: Stand-in experiment on OpenML Adult (ID 1590). Records split 60/20/20 (train/validation/test), one-hot encoded. A LightGBM attacker learns real records vs random population decoys and, for each bin (real record + decoys), picks the top-scoring member. Same attacker in all conditions.
baseline: Fixed bin size 16 (common default, not from the paper) with the same LightGBM attacker.
improved: Bin size chosen as the smallest in [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64] whose validation top-1 rate is <= 0.1; falls back to the largest size if none qualifies.
notes: Stand-in for the paper's ledger, not a re-implementation. Decoys are drawn attribute-by-attribute from population marginals, so the attacker exploits broken correlations (e.g. education vs education-num). Bin-size selection uses a held-out validation split (not k-fold CV) because the rule is defined on validation top-1; the test set is used once per seed. Attacker hyper-parameters are fixed, not tuned. Std is population std over seeds 42-44 (attacker and bin randomness; one data split). Storage overhead is the bin size. Fix: nominal-column detection now uses is_numeric_dtype instead of dtype==object, so it works with pandas 3 string dtypes.
